# CardDemo parity oracle audit

This audit records what the COBOL oracle does, so that the Rust and web replacement can be written and tested against it. Each row is one decision of a carried program, copybook, JCL step or fixture, cited to the physical lines it comes from. Defect-like behaviour is recorded as the COBOL performs it; anomalous fixtures are read as their bytes say. Rows whose result cannot be pinned from the repository and IBM documentation name a `halt` escalation instead of a guess.

Author: `blitzy-audit-author`. Reviewer of every row: `blitzy-cobol-reviewer`. Escalations raised here are listed in the last section and carried into `docs/parity/escalations.md`; the human COBOL review the request names is tracked in `docs/parity/signoff.md`.

## Gates

A file gated by a section is written only when every row of that section has passed its review log.

| Section | Content | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| A. Record layouts | one row per elementary field of every record layout, FILLER included | crates/domain/src/numeric/**, crates/codec/src/layouts/**, migrations/0001 to 0004, crates/persistence/src/seed.rs |
| B. Per-program rules | paragraph decisions, key paths, file access, write persistence | crates/domain/src/rules/**, crates/domain/src/messages.rs, crates/domain/src/format.rs, crates/api/src/handlers/** (except rewards.rs and admin_reward_rules.rs), crates/batch/src/jobs/{posttran,intcalc,tranbkp,combtran,creastmt,tranrept,cbpaup0j,mnttrdb2}.rs, crates/messaging/src/flows/**, crates/messaging/src/error_queue.rs, every parity test |
| C. Arithmetic | receivers, truncation, worked values | as section B |
| D. Fixture expectations | results of the audited rules on the fixture corpus | as section B |
| E. Anomalies | defect-like paths and anomalous fixtures with their disposition | as section B |
| F. Time-dependent fields | formats of clock-dependent output | as section B |

## Conventions

- Tables are GitHub pipe tables, one record per line; a literal `|` inside a cell is written `\|`.
- Row IDs are `P-<KEY>-<nnn>`; `<KEY>` equals the row's Program cell, and numbering per key runs continuously through sections A to F.
- Citations are `[<path>:L<n>]`, `[<path>:L<n>-<m>]` or `[<path>]`, with repository-relative paths in their stored case and 1-based physical line numbers of the stored file (never the COBOL sequence numbers in columns 1-6 or 73-80). Every data row carries at least one `path:L<n>` citation (`[<path>:L<n>]` or `[<path>:L<n>-<m>]`); a bare `[<path>]` is supplementary only and never a row's sole citation. Every Paragraph cell carries at least one citation. IBM manuals are cited by title in plain text.
- Byte offsets are 0-based; lengths are in bytes.
- An exact text is a code span holding a double-quoted string, with `\"` and `\\` as escapes; `width=<n>` after it means the value is right-padded with spaces to n bytes. `{FIELD}` stands for the content of that COBOL field in a STRING-built text, `{UNDEF:n}` for n bytes the COBOL never sets.
- Structured results are `key=value; key=value`, values being bare tokens or exact texts.
- Escalation IDs: E-01 to E-22 are the seeded log of `docs/parity/escalations.md`; E-23 onward are raised in the last section of this file.
- Persists on later failure: `persists: RECOVERY(NONE)` for VSAM writes [app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:L1-96], or the commit or rollback the program issues for Db2 and IMS writes; `n/a` where a path has at most one write.

## A. Record layouts

Codec facts confirmed against the bytes: every signed DISPLAY field in the nine ASCII fixture files uses a trailing overpunch (`{ABCDEFGHI` for +0 to +9, `}JKLMNOPQR` for -0 to -9); the twelve codec layouts (the nine fixture copybooks, CSUSR01Y, the reject record and CVTRA05Y as the transaction output) have no COMP, COMP-3, REDEFINES or OCCURS; the FILLER of DISCGRP, TCATBAL, TRANTYPE and TRANCATG holds the character 0. No contrary byte was found.

## D. Fixture expectations

### D.1 POSTTRAN reject set

Keys: record_no, tran_id, reason, description, bytes, card, account_id, ws_temp_bal, acct_credit_limit, acct_expiraion_date, orig_date, read, posted, rejected, exit

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. POSTTRAN runs CBTRN02C over all 300 records of dailytran.txt with the clock pinned to 2022-07-01T12:00:00Z; validation order 100, 101, 102, 103 (103 overwrites 102); accepted records update the cycle totals before the next record is checked. Every reject of the corpus is reason 0102: the 103 test passes for all of them. Used by crates/batch/tests/posttran_rejects.rs.

### D.3 INTCALC

Keys: account_id, tran_type_cd, tran_cat_cd, group, rate, tran_cat_bal, monthly_interest, tran_id, total_interest, updated, acct_curr_bal, acct_curr_cyc_credit, acct_curr_cyc_debit, systran_tran_id, card_number, kind, records, first, last

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. INTCALC runs CBACT04C with --parm-date 2022071800 [app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:L22] over the category balances after POSTTRAN (D.2), in key order. Every ACCT-GROUP-ID is blank (E-06), so every rate comes from the DEFAULT group.

### D.4 COMBTRAN

Keys: records, order, first, last, equal_keys, loaded, rejected, stopped_at, not_attempted, exit, live_master

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after POSTTRAN (D.1), INTCALC (D.3) and TRANBKP; the combined file is backup(0) followed by SYSTRAN(0), sorted by TRAN-ID. Interleaved rows apply the REPRO duplicate-key rows of section B (COMBTRAN STEP10) to the combined record numbers given; the corpus itself never reaches that case, because CT02 and CB00 cannot add to an empty live master (E-27).

### D.5 CREASTMT

Keys: cards, max_transactions_per_card, transactions, within_capacity, file, name, records, width, terminator, card_order, per_card_records, kind, line_no, text, card_number, account_id, customer_id, n

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after POSTTRAN, INTCALC, TRANBKP and COMBTRAN [README.md:L224-228]. A card statement has n transaction lines, n being its kind=card_summary row. Template rows hold for every card: in line_no, n is that count and i runs from 1 to n. Variable rows give the absolute line number within the card. Cards follow in card-number order. {UNDEF:k} stands for k bytes the COBOL never sets (E-25): the replacement writes spaces there, which also keeps the HTML STRING DELIMITED BY '*' from stopping early.

### D.6 TRANREPT

Keys: records_in_range, lines, width, terminator, order, line_no, kind, text, tran_id, total

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after batch seed and batch posttran with CARDDEMO_CLOCK_OVERRIDE=2022-07-01T12:00:00Z, so every posted record carries PROC-TS 2022-07-01 and falls inside 2022-01-01..2022-07-06; tranrept backs up the live master, keeps the in-range records, sorts them by card number and runs CBTRN03C.

### D.10 CP00 examples

Keys: kind, available, request, reply, reply_length, auth_resp_code, auth_resp_reason, approved_amt, database_writes

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. Requests are CCPAURQY comma-separated texts against the seeded state (no pending-authorization summary exists, so the available amount is ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT - ACCT-CURR-BAL); the 64-byte reply is the 63 STRING bytes plus one byte never set.
